title: Canada Express Entry from 3 November 2026: new points for high-wage jobs, no LMIA needed
description: From 3 November 2026, Express Entry gives up to 100 extra points for a job offer in a high-wage occupation, and the offer no longer needs an LMIA. Here's who gains and what to do now.

facts.label: Starts
facts.value: 3 November 2026

facts.label: Job offer points
facts.value: 50, 70 or 100, depending on the occupation's wage level

facts.label: Canadian experience points
facts.value: 20, 40 or 70 extra after 12 months in a high-wage job

facts.label: LMIA
facts.value: No longer needed for a qualifying job offer

body:
Express Entry is Canada’s main system for skilled workers who want permanent residence. On 16 October 2026, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) announced the biggest change to its scoring in more than a year. From 3 November 2026, candidates with a job offer or Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation get extra points, and a qualifying job offer no longer needs a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA).

Here’s how it works, and what it means if you’re applying from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe or Zambia.

How Express Entry works

Express Entry covers three programmes:

  • Federal Skilled Worker Program: the one most people abroad use. You need at least one year of continuous skilled work in the last 10 years, a language score of at least CLB 7, your education assessed, 67 points on the programme’s grid and proof of funds.
  • Canadian Experience Class: for people who already have skilled work experience in Canada.
  • Federal Skilled Trades Program: for trades such as electricians, welders and plumbers.

You create a profile and get a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score out of 1,200. IRCC then holds draws and invites the highest-scoring candidates to apply for permanent residence. Some draws are open to everyone; others are for categories such as health care, skilled trades and education.

What changes on 3 November 2026

Points for a job offer in a high-wage occupation

Since March 2025, a job offer gave you no CRS points at all. From 3 November 2026, a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation earns points again:

  • 100 points if the occupation’s median wage is at least 2 times the average median wage in Canada.
  • 70 points if it’s at least 1.5 times.
  • 50 points if it’s at least 1.3 times.

The offer must generally be for full-time, continuous work in Canada for at least one year after you become a permanent resident. It doesn’t need an LMIA, but IRCC still checks that it’s genuine: that the employer is a real, active business, needs the role, can pay you and follows employment law. A job offer that’s withdrawn no longer counts.

Points for Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation

If you already have at least 12 months of skilled work in Canada in a high-wage occupation, you get 70, 40 or 20 extra points, using the same 2, 1.5 and 1.3 times tiers. These come on top of the normal points for Canadian experience.

You get either the job offer points or the experience points, whichever is higher. They aren’t added together. The total for this part of your score is capped at 150 points, or 140 if your spouse or partner is coming with you.

Job offers for the Federal Skilled Worker and Trades programmes

A temporary policy also removes the LMIA requirement for job offers used to qualify for the Federal Skilled Worker and Federal Skilled Trades programmes, for candidates invited on or after 3 November 2026 who meet its conditions.

Which jobs count as high-wage

The list goes by your occupation’s code (NOC) and the national median wage for that occupation, not your own salary. It covers sectors such as engineering, technology, health care, education, management and skilled trades. Software developers, engineers, data scientists, registered nurses, accountants and electricians are among the occupations on it.

Find your NOC code first, then check which tier it’s in on IRCC’s high-wage occupations list.

What it means if you’re applying from Africa

  • The Canadian experience points won’t help you yet, because they need 12 months of work inside Canada.
  • A genuine job offer can now add 50 to 100 points, without your employer going through the LMIA process. That makes it easier for Canadian employers to hire you in a high-wage occupation.
  • More points don’t guarantee an invitation. Each draw has its own cut-off score.
  • Never pay for a job offer. Expect a wave of people selling “LMIA-free job offers”. IRCC checks every offer, and lying on an application can get you banned from applying for 5 years. Here’s how to spot fake job and visa offers.

What to do now

If you’re already in the pool and have a job offer, update your profile with all the job offer details before 3 November 2026. IRCC will recalculate everyone’s scores, which can take up to two weeks, and it’s pausing invitation rounds while it does.

If you’re not in the pool yet, get the basics ready:

  1. Get an Educational Credential Assessment for your degree. See how the ECA and WES work.
  2. Take an English test IRCC accepts: IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General or PTE Core. The Duolingo English Test doesn’t count for Express Entry. See Duolingo or IELTS.
  3. Check you have the proof of funds below.
  4. Work out your NOC code and whether it’s on the high-wage list.

Proof of funds

Federal Skilled Worker and Federal Skilled Trades candidates must show they have at least this much, in Canadian dollars:

Family membersFunds you need
1CAD 15,263
2CAD 19,001
3CAD 23,360
4CAD 28,362
5CAD 32,168

You don’t need proof of funds if you’re applying through the Canadian Experience Class, or if you’re authorised to work in Canada and have a valid job offer. These are the amounts on IRCC’s page in October 2026, and IRCC updates them every year.

Canada isn’t the only option. Compare it with Germany, Ireland and Australia in moving abroad beyond Canada.

title: How to write a CV for jobs abroad: UK, Canada and Germany compared
description: A CV that works in Lagos, Accra or Nairobi can cost you interviews in London, Toronto or Berlin. Here's what to include, what to leave out and how long it should be in each country.

facts.label: UK
facts.value: No age, date of birth, marital status or nationality

facts.label: Canada
facts.value: Two pages at most, no photo, age or marital status

facts.label: Germany
facts.value: A table-style CV, and a photo is often expected

facts.label: Free tool
facts.value: Europass builds a CV and cover letter for you

body:
Most CVs written for jobs in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe or Zambia follow local habits: a photo, date of birth, marital status, state of origin, a long career objective and four or five pages. Employers abroad expect something very different, and a CV that looks wrong to them often isn’t read to the end.

Here’s how to change your CV for the UK, Canada and Germany, using each country’s own official advice.

What to change for any country

  • Cut the personal details. Date of birth, age, marital status, religion, state of origin and number of children don’t belong on a CV for the UK or Canada. They invite bias, and employers there don’t expect to see them.
  • Replace the “career objective” with a short profile. Three or four lines on who you are, what you’re good at and what you want next.
  • Lead with achievements, not duties. “Cut customer complaints by 30% in six months” beats “Responsible for customer service”.
  • Put your most recent job first, and give the most space to the last 10 to 15 years.
  • Keep school history short. Your degree and professional qualifications matter; primary school doesn’t.
  • Say if you need a visa. A line such as “Open to relocation; will need Skilled Worker visa sponsorship” saves time for you and the employer.

The UK

The UK’s National Careers Service says a CV should have:

  • contact details: your name, phone number, email address and a LinkedIn link if you have one,
  • a short introduction or personal profile,
  • your work history,
  • your education,
  • references, which are optional. Only include people who’ve agreed to act as one.

It also says you shouldn’t include your age, date of birth, whether you’re married or your nationality. UK CVs normally don’t have a photo either. Two pages is the usual length.

If you’re applying for a sponsored job, check the employer is a licensed sponsor first. See the UK Skilled Worker visa rules.

Canada

In Canada it’s called a resume. The Government of Canada’s Job Bank advises:

  • two pages at most,
  • your name, address, email and phone number at the top of the first page,
  • achievements under each job, with 5 to 7 bullet points per section at most,
  • volunteer work, especially if it relates to the job,
  • cutting or shortening experience that’s more than 15 years old.

Job Bank says a photo “is not the norm in Canada” and can lower your chances. Leave out your age, weight, height and marital status too.

Planning to move through Express Entry? Read what changes on 3 November 2026.

Germany

German employers expect a more formal application. Make it in Germany, the government’s site for skilled workers, says:

  • the CV (Lebenslauf) is usually laid out as a table, with your most recent job and education first,
  • employers often expect a photo, though this varies by industry,
  • your cover letter should introduce you, say why you want this job at this company, and show your strengths with examples from past jobs,
  • you should attach your certificates and diplomas and any references from past employers,
  • certificates should be translated into German or English,
  • applications usually go by email as one PDF, or through the company’s careers site.

Germany also checks that your qualification is recognised for many jobs. Read how Germany’s skilled worker routes work and our EU Blue Card guide.

A free tool: Europass

Europass is the European Union’s free tool for building a CV and cover letter. You fill in a profile once and it turns it into a clean CV you can download. Make it in Germany suggests it as a starting point, but adapt the design so your CV doesn’t look exactly like everyone else’s. Europass also has job and course searches across Europe.

How to write a strong achievement line

Use this pattern: action + what you did + result.

  • “Led a team of 6 engineers to deliver a billing system two months early.”
  • “Trained 120 new staff across 4 branches, cutting onboarding time from 3 weeks to 10 days.”
  • “Grew the company’s Instagram audience from 2,000 to 25,000 in a year.”

If you can’t give a number, give the scale: how many people, branches, customers or projects.

Be honest

Never invent jobs, degrees or references. Employers abroad check them, and so do visa officers. A fake certificate can end an application and get you banned from a country. Read how to spot fake job and visa offers too, because scammers often ask for your CV first.

title: EU Blue Card Germany 2026: salary rules, shortage jobs and fast permanent residence
description: Germany's EU Blue Card needs a degree and a job paying €50,700, or €45,934.20 in shortage jobs. IT specialists can qualify without a degree. Here's how it works in 2026.

facts.label: Salary
facts.value: €50,700 a year, or €45,934.20 in shortage jobs and for recent graduates

facts.label: Degree
facts.value: A German or comparable foreign degree. IT specialists can use 3 years' experience instead

facts.label: Permanent residence
facts.value: After 27 months, or 21 months with B1 German

facts.label: Lasts
facts.value: Your contract plus 6 months, up to 4 years at a time

body:
The EU Blue Card is Germany’s main work permit for graduates, and its rules have become more flexible in recent years. The salary you need is far lower than in the Netherlands, IT specialists can qualify without a degree, and you can get permanent residence in as little as 21 months.

Here’s how it works for applicants from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia.

Who can get one

You need all of these:

  • A degree from a German university, or a foreign degree that’s comparable to a German one. A tertiary qualification of at least three years at level 6 of the European framework can also count.
  • A job offer in Germany for at least 6 months.
  • A job that matches your qualification.
  • A salary that meets the 2026 threshold below.
  • A licence to practise, or the prospect of one, if your profession is regulated, such as doctors and nurses.

You don’t need to speak German for the Blue Card itself, although many employers will ask for it.

Salary thresholds in 2026

WhoMinimum gross salary a year
Most jobs€50,700
Shortage occupations€45,934.20
Recent graduates (degree less than 3 years old)€45,934.20
IT specialists without a degree€45,934.20

For shortage occupations and recent graduates on the lower salary, the Federal Employment Agency must also approve the job.

Shortage occupations

The lower salary applies to jobs including:

  • managers in manufacturing, mining, construction and distribution,
  • ICT service managers,
  • managers in childcare, health and education services,
  • academic STEM professionals, such as engineers and scientists,
  • architects and planners,
  • doctors, vets, dentists and pharmacists,
  • academic nursing and midwifery professionals,
  • teachers and educators.

IT specialists without a degree

You can get a Blue Card without a degree if you have:

  • an IT job offer for at least 6 months,
  • a salary of at least €45,934.20,
  • at least 3 years of IT experience in the last 7 years, at a level comparable to a university graduate.

Check your degree is recognised

Before you apply, check that your university and degree are listed as comparable in the anabin database of the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB). If your degree isn’t listed clearly, apply to the ZAB for a Statement of Comparability. Make it in Germany’s recognition finder tells you if your profession needs full recognition too.

How long it lasts, and permanent residence

Your Blue Card lasts for your contract plus 6 months, up to 4 years, and you can extend it in Germany.

You can apply for a settlement permit, which is permanent residence, after:

  • 27 months with basic German (level A1), or
  • 21 months with intermediate German (level B1).

Bringing your family

Your spouse and children can join you. Spouses of Blue Card holders don’t have to prove German before they come, and they can work in Germany.

Changing jobs

You can move to a new job on your Blue Card. If you change jobs in your first year, you must tell your local foreigners authority, which checks you still meet the Blue Card conditions.

How to apply

  1. Get the job offer and a signed contract.
  2. Check your degree is comparable, as above.
  3. Book a national visa appointment at the German embassy or consulate in your country. Many use a visa centre to take applications.
  4. Bring your passport, contract, degree certificates, CV and proof of health insurance.
  5. Once you’re in Germany, register your address and apply for the Blue Card at the foreigners authority.

Your employer can also start the fast-track procedure for skilled workers at the foreigners authority in Germany, which speeds up the embassy appointment and decision.

Blue Card or another route?

  • No job offer yet? The Opportunity Card lets you go to Germany for up to a year to look for one.
  • Vocational qualification instead of a degree? See the other skilled worker routes and Ausbildung.
  • Comparing countries? The Netherlands asks for €5,942 a month for its Blue Card. See the Dutch highly skilled migrant permit.

Write your CV the German way before you apply. Here’s how to write a CV for Germany, the UK and Canada.

title: Netherlands highly skilled migrant visa 2026: salary rules, fees and how it works
description: The Netherlands lets recognised employers hire skilled workers from Africa with one permit. Here are the 2026 salary thresholds (€5,942 or €4,357 a month), the €423 fee and the steps.

facts.label: Salary if you're 30 or older
facts.value: €5,942 a month before tax

facts.label: Salary if you're under 30
facts.value: €4,357 a month before tax

facts.label: Recent graduates
facts.value: €3,122 a month, if you qualify for the reduced criterion

facts.label: Fee
facts.value: €423, plus €254 for a partner and €85 for a child

body:
The Netherlands has one of Europe’s simplest routes for skilled workers: the highly skilled migrant permit, often called the kennismigrant scheme. Your employer applies for you, the main test is your salary, and your partner can come with you.

Here’s how it works in 2026 for people from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia.

Who can use it

You need:

  • a job offer and employment contract from an employer the IND has approved as a recognised sponsor. Only these employers can apply for this permit, and they’re listed in the IND’s public register of recognised sponsors;
  • a salary that meets the 2026 threshold for your age, shown below;
  • a salary that’s in line with the market rate for the job.

The IND’s main tests are the employer and the salary, so check both before you spend time on an application.

Salary thresholds for 2026

These are gross monthly amounts, before tax and without holiday pay:

WhoMinimum gross salary a month
30 or older€5,942
Under 30€4,357
Reduced criterion (recent graduates)€3,122

The amounts change every 1 January, and the one that counts is the amount on the day your employer applies. If you were under 30 when you first got the permit, the lower amount still applies at your extension with the same employer. If you change employer, your age when the new contract starts decides which amount applies.

The lower salary for recent graduates

The reduced amount of €3,122 applies if you have, or qualify for, the Netherlands’ orientation year permit for highly educated people, and your employer applies within 3 years of your graduation. For graduates from outside the Netherlands, that generally means:

  • a master’s, PhD or post-master’s degree,
  • from a university in the top 200 of the general or subject rankings of at least two of Times Higher Education, QS and ShanghaiRanking,
  • earned within the last 3 years.

Graduates of Dutch universities and Erasmus Mundus joint master’s programmes also qualify. The IND asks for a Nuffic evaluation of foreign diplomas. Ask the IND if you’re unsure whether your degree counts.

EU Blue Card in the Netherlands

The Netherlands also issues the EU Blue Card, which needs a higher education degree. In 2026 it needs a salary of €5,942 a month, or €4,754 under the reduced criterion. Germany’s Blue Card asks for much less. Compare it in our EU Blue Card Germany guide.

How to apply

Your employer does most of the work:

  1. Your employer checks you meet the conditions and collects your documents.
  2. Your employer applies to the IND, usually online, and pays the fee.
  3. The IND decides.
  4. If it’s approved, you book an appointment at the Dutch embassy or consulate for your MVV (an entry visa sticker) and travel to the Netherlands.
  5. You collect your residence permit in the Netherlands.

You may need a TB test at the local health service (GGD) within 3 months of getting your permit. If the decision says so, you can start work before you have the permit card, but you must book your biometrics appointment within 2 weeks of your employer receiving the decision.

Fees in 2026

  • €423 for the highly skilled migrant permit.
  • €254 for a partner.
  • €85 for a child under 18.

How long it lasts

The permit lasts as long as your contract, up to 5 years, and your employer can apply to extend it. After 5 years you can apply for permanent residence, if you meet the other conditions.

If you lose your job, you have 3 months to find a new one with a recognised sponsor. If you’ve had the permit for at least 2 years and became unemployed on or after 22 May 2026, you get up to 6 months.

Bringing your family

Your partner and children can apply through your employer at the same time as you. Partners of highly skilled migrants are allowed to work in the Netherlands.

Where to find employers

Search the IND’s register of recognised sponsors for companies in your field, then look for their jobs on their own sites and on LinkedIn. Technology, engineering, finance and research employers are among those that hire from abroad.

Never pay anyone to “arrange” a Dutch work permit. Only the employer can apply. Read how to spot fake job and visa offers.

title: SI Scholarship for Global Professionals 2027: a funded master's in Sweden
description: The Swedish Institute pays tuition, SEK 12,000 a month and a travel grant for a master's in Sweden. Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Zambia are eligible. Apply to universities by 15 January 2027.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: One- or two-year master's at a Swedish university

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: Full tuition, SEK 12,000 a month to live on and a SEK 15,000 travel grant

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Citizens of 34 countries, including Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Zambia

facts.label: Deadlines
facts.value: Universities by 15 January 2027, then the scholarship from 9 to 25 February 2027

body:
The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is the Swedish government’s main scholarship for master’s students from outside Europe. It’s run by the Swedish Institute (SI) and it’s aimed at people who already have work and leadership experience and want to bring new skills back to their country.

For courses starting in autumn 2027, there are two deadlines, and the first one is 15 January 2027.

What it pays

  • Full tuition fees, paid by SI straight to your university each semester.
  • SEK 12,000 a month for living costs.
  • A one-off travel grant of SEK 15,000.
  • Membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals, and the Sweden Alumni Network afterwards.

Insurance isn’t part of the scholarship, so check what cover your university gives international students.

Who can apply

You must be a citizen of one of 34 eligible countries. Where you live now doesn’t matter. The African countries on the list are:

Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Morocco, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia.

Ghana and Zimbabwe aren’t eligible this round. If that’s you, look at our 2027 scholarship calendar, Erasmus Mundus or DAAD EPOS in Germany instead.

You also need:

  • Work experience you can prove. SI sets the minimum in its application documents, so check it before you apply.
  • Leadership experience, from your current or past job, from running your own business, or from community and civil society work.
  • To be someone who pays tuition fees in Sweden, which applies to most people from outside the EU.
  • To be admitted to an eligible master’s programme by the time university results come out.

The 2027 timeline

DateWhat happens
16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027Apply to master’s programmes at universityadmissions.se
9 to 25 February 2027Apply for the SI scholarship on SI’s portal
26 March 2027University admission results
23 April 2027SI scholarship results
August 2027Courses start

SI publishes the list of eligible programmes before the scholarship opens, so check that your programmes are on it when you choose them. On universityadmissions.se you can list up to four programmes in one application.

When you apply to the universities you get an eight-digit application number. You’ll need it for the SI application, and a wrong number gets you disqualified.

How to make your application stand out

  • Show real leadership. Name the team you led, the project you ran or the group you started, and what changed because of it. Numbers help: “trained 40 health workers” says more than “passionate about health”.
  • Connect the degree to your career. Explain what you’ll do with it when you’re back home, and why this programme in Sweden is the right one.
  • Get your proof of work ready early. Employer letters should give your job title, dates and hours.
  • Write your own motivation letters. Our statement of purpose guide works for these too.
  • Prepare your English test. Most Swedish master’s programmes ask for an English score unless your degree was taught in English. See IELTS or Duolingo.

Common mistakes

  • Missing the 15 January university deadline. Without it, you can’t apply for the scholarship in February.
  • Choosing a programme that isn’t on SI’s eligible list.
  • Typing the application number wrong.
  • Leaving the work and leadership sections vague.

title: UK Student visa 2026: costs, documents and the money you must show
description: A UK Student visa costs £558 plus £776 a year for the health surcharge. Here's how much money you must show, the documents you need, the TB test and who can still bring family.

facts.label: Visa fee
facts.value: £558 when you apply from outside the UK

facts.label: Health surcharge
facts.value: £776 for each year of your visa

facts.label: Money to show
facts.value: £1,529 a month in London or £1,171 elsewhere, for up to 9 months, plus your fees

facts.label: Decision
facts.value: Usually within 3 weeks

body:
The UK is still one of the most popular places for students from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia to study. A one-year master’s gets you a degree fast, and the Graduate visa lets you stay and work afterwards.

But the Student visa has costs people underestimate. Here’s what you’ll pay, what you must show and how to get it right first time.

What you need before you apply

  • An unconditional offer from a university that’s a licensed student sponsor. The university then gives you a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) number.
  • English at level B2 for a degree course. Your university can assess this itself, or ask you for an approved test such as IELTS for UKVI.
  • Money for your fees and living costs, held for 28 days (see below).
  • A TB test certificate (see below).
  • A valid passport.

What it costs

CostAmount
Visa fee, applying from outside the UK£558
Immigration health surcharge£776 a year
Each family member who comes with you£558 visa fee plus £776 a year

The surcharge depends on the length of your visa, not your course. A visa for more than a year but no more than 18 months costs £1,164 in surcharge; a visa for more than 18 months but under 2 years costs £1,552. A one-year master’s usually gets a visa of around 16 to 17 months, because it includes extra time after the course ends, so most master’s students pay £1,164.

You also pay for the TB test and, if your university asks for it, an English test.

How much money you must show

You need to show your unpaid course fees for the first year, plus living costs of:

  • £1,529 a month if you’ll study in London, for up to 9 months: £13,761.
  • £1,171 a month anywhere else in the UK, for up to 9 months: £10,539.

If your family comes with you, add £845 a month for each person in London, or £680 elsewhere, for up to 9 months.

The money must sit in your account for at least 28 days in a row, and the end of that 28-day period must be within 31 days of the day you apply. Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia aren’t on the UK’s reduced-evidence list, so you must send the bank statements with your application.

You don’t need to show living costs if you’ve already lived in the UK on a valid visa for 12 months or more. Our proof of funds guide explains which statements and sponsor letters UKVI accepts.

The TB test

If you’re applying from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe or Zambia, you need a tuberculosis test from a clinic approved by the UK Home Office. Book it early, because you need the certificate before you apply, and only approved clinics count.

Can you bring your family?

Only some students can:

  • students on a PhD, other doctorate or research-based master’s course,
  • government-sponsored students on a course longer than 6 months.

If you’re starting a taught master’s or an undergraduate degree, you can’t bring your partner or children on your Student visa.

When to apply and how long it takes

  • From outside the UK, you can apply up to 6 months before your course starts.
  • You give your fingerprints and photo at a visa application centre.
  • You’ll usually get a decision within 3 weeks.

Apply as soon as you have your CAS and your money has been in your account for 28 days. September intakes are the busiest time.

Working while you study

At degree level you can work up to 20 hours a week during term time, and full-time in the holidays. Many students use this for living costs, but you can’t count future earnings as your proof of funds.

After you graduate

The Graduate visa lets you stay and work after your degree. It’s getting shorter: people who apply from 1 January 2027 get 18 months instead of 2 years. See what the Graduate visa change means for you, and the Skilled Worker visa rules if you want to stay longer.

Looking for funding first? Chevening, Commonwealth and Gates Cambridge are in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

title: Canada ECA for Express Entry: WES cost, documents and the 5-year rule
description: Express Entry needs an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) for any degree you earned outside Canada. Here's who issues it, what WES charges, how to send your documents and how long it stays valid.

facts.label: Who needs it
facts.value: Anyone using a degree from outside Canada for Express Entry

facts.label: Valid for
facts.value: 5 years from the date it's issued

facts.label: WES fee
facts.value: CAD 264, plus delivery and tax where it applies

facts.label: Your spouse
facts.value: Can get an ECA too and add points to your score

body:
If you plan to move to Canada through Express Entry, your degree from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa or anywhere else outside Canada has to be checked first. That check is called an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA). It shows Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) what your qualification is worth in Canada.

Who needs an ECA

You need one if you completed your education outside Canada and you want to:

  • qualify for the Federal Skilled Worker Program as the main applicant, or
  • get points for your education in your Express Entry score.

Your spouse or partner can get an ECA too. If they’re coming with you, their education can add points to your score.

Degrees from Canadian schools don’t need an ECA.

Who can issue it

Most people use one of these five organisations:

  • World Education Services (WES)
  • International Credential Assessment Service of Canada (ICAS)
  • International Qualifications Assessment Service (IQAS)
  • International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES)
  • Comparative Education Service (University of Toronto)

Some professions must use their professional body instead:

  • Doctors (specialists and family physicians): Medical Council of Canada.
  • Pharmacists who need a licence: Pharmacy Examining Board of Canada.
  • Architects who need a licence: Canadian Architectural Certification Board.

Whichever you choose, ask for an ECA for immigration purposes. A general evaluation won’t count for Express Entry.

How much WES charges

  • CAD 264 for the ECA.
  • Delivery: CAD 14 for standard post without tracking, or CAD 97 for international courier.
  • 13% sales tax (HST) where it applies.

You’ll also pay your university for your transcript and for sending it, and that fee depends on your school.

How to send your documents

WES is strict about where documents come from. For most degrees:

  1. Create your WES account and pay. You get a WES reference number.
  2. In your account, open View Required Documents to see exactly what your school must send.
  3. Ask your university to send your transcript in a sealed envelope straight to WES, with your reference number.
  4. Upload or send a copy of your degree certificate yourself, if your school is on the list that needs one.

For example, University of Ibadan graduates ask the university to send the transcript and the WES Academic Records Request Form together in a sealed envelope, and send a photocopy of their degree certificate themselves. Every school is different, so always check your own list.

Transcripts from some universities can take weeks to arrive, so start the request as early as you can.

The 5-year rule

Your ECA must be less than 5 years old:

  • when you create your Express Entry profile,
  • for the whole time your profile is in the pool, and
  • when you submit your application after an invitation.

If it expires, your application can be refused. If your ECA is getting old, get a new one before you’re invited.

What to do next

Get your language test done while you wait for the ECA. Express Entry only accepts certain English tests, and the Duolingo English Test isn’t one of them. See Duolingo vs IELTS and the IELTS fee in Nigeria.

Not sure Canada is right for you? Compare it with other countries in moving abroad: look beyond Canada.

title: Chevening 2027/28: what happens after you apply, and how to prepare for the next round
description: Chevening applications for 2027/28 closed in October 2026. Here's the timeline to results in June 2027, what to do while you wait, and how to get ready if you plan to apply in 2027.

facts.label: Interviews
facts.value: March to April 2027

facts.label: Results
facts.value: From mid-June 2027

facts.label: Offer deadline
facts.value: Unconditional university offer by 8 July 2027, 17:00 UK time

facts.label: Work experience
facts.value: At least 2 years (2,800 hours) after your first degree

body:
Chevening is the UK government’s scholarship for a fully funded one-year master’s degree at a UK university. Applications for the 2027/28 intake ran from August to October 2026 and are now closed.

If you applied, here’s what happens next. If you missed it, the second half of this post shows how to be ready for the next round.

The 2027/28 timeline

WhenWhat happens
From October 2026Applications are checked against the eligibility rules
Mid-October 2026 to January 2027Reading committees assess applications
Mid-February 2027British embassies and high commissions shortlist people for interview
March to April 2027Interviews at the British embassy or high commission
From mid-June 2027Results
8 July 2027, 17:00 UK timeDeadline to send at least one unconditional university offer
September or October 2027Studies begin in the UK

What to do while you wait

1. Work on your university offers now. This is where many people lose their award. You applied for three UK courses, and you must have an unconditional offer from at least one of them by 8 July 2027. An unconditional offer means you’ve met every condition, including the university’s English requirement. Book your English test early if your universities ask for one. See Duolingo vs IELTS to check which tests your universities accept.

2. Get your documents ready. If you’re shortlisted, you must upload these at least 7 working days before your interview:

  • photo ID,
  • your undergraduate degree certificate or diploma,
  • your reference letters.

You need your degree certificate by the interview, so request it from your university now if you don’t have it.

3. Prepare for the interview. Re-read your application essays, because the panel uses them. Practise explaining your leadership examples, your career plan and how the course will help you make a difference at home.

Eligibility, for anyone applying next time

To apply, you must:

  • be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country,
  • agree to return to your country for at least 2 years after your scholarship ends,
  • have an undergraduate degree that gets you into a UK master’s, finished at least 2 years before the application deadline,
  • have at least 2 years (2,800 hours) of work experience after your undergraduate degree,
  • apply to three different eligible UK courses.

There’s no upper age limit. Having a master’s degree already doesn’t stop you from applying.

You can’t apply if you hold British or dual British citizenship, live in the UK when you apply, or have already studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship. People who work for (or recently worked for) a UK government department or the British Council, and their close relatives, can’t apply either.

How to prepare for the next round

If the next round follows this year’s pattern, applications will open around August 2027 and close in October 2027. Use the time before then:

  1. Count your work hours. Make sure you’ll have 2,800 hours after your degree by the deadline.
  2. Pick your three courses and check their entry requirements now.
  3. Draft your essays early. Our statement of purpose guide shows how to tell your story clearly.
  4. Line up two referees who know your work well.

Because you agree to go home after your course, Chevening isn’t a route to staying in the UK on a Graduate visa. If you want to stay and work, look at other options. Our list of fully funded scholarships for Africans shows what’s open now.

title: Ausbildung in Germany: paid vocational training for Africans in 2026
description: With an Ausbildung you train for a skilled job in Germany and earn a monthly allowance while you learn. Here are the 2026 rules: German level, money you must show, the search visa and what happens after you qualify.

facts.label: German
facts.value: B1 usually required

facts.label: Money to show
facts.value: €822 net (€1,048 gross) a month for company training in 2026

facts.label: After training
facts.value: Up to 18 months to find a job, then settlement after 2 years of work

body:
An Ausbildung is Germany’s vocational training. You sign a training contract with a German company, learn the job there, and spend part of the week at a vocational school. You’re paid a training allowance every month, and at the end you get a German qualification.

It’s one of the best routes to Germany if you don’t have a university degree. Training programmes usually last 2 to 3.5 years. Common fields include nursing and elderly care, electrical work, plumbing and heating, hotels and restaurants, and logistics.

What you need for the training visa

  • A training contract or confirmed training place with a German company.
  • German at B1 level, unless the company has tested your German itself.
  • Proof you can support yourself. For company training in 2026, that’s at least €822 net (€1,048 gross) a month. If your training pay is lower, ask the German embassy how to show the difference, for example with a blocked account.
  • Valid health insurance.
  • Your passport and original documents.

For school-based training, where you train at a school instead of a company, you must show at least €959 net a month. You can do this with a blocked account, a scholarship or a formal Declaration of Commitment from someone in Germany.

The Federal Employment Agency also checks that you’ll be trained and paid on the same terms as German trainees. The embassy arranges this, so you don’t need to do anything.

Fees: the visa costs €75, paid in local currency. Your residence permit in Germany can cost up to €100 more.

No training place yet? Use the search visa

Germany has a separate visa to come and look for a training place. You need:

  • to be 35 or younger,
  • German at B1 level or higher,
  • a school-leaving certificate that lets you go to university in Germany or in your home country,
  • a blocked account with at least €1,091 a month (2026 figure), a scholarship or a Declaration of Commitment,
  • health insurance.

You can stay up to 9 months while you search. You may work up to 20 hours a week and do up to 2 weeks of trial work with companies.

During your training

Your residence permit lasts as long as your training. You can take a side job of up to 20 hours a week, as long as it isn’t part of your training.

After you qualify

  • You can stay up to 18 months to find a job in your field. For care and health assistant training, it’s up to 12 months, which can be extended once by 6 months.
  • While you look, you can take any job to pay your bills.
  • After 2 years of work following your training, you may be able to get a settlement permit, which is permanent residence, if you meet the other conditions.

How to find a training place

  1. Learn German to B1. Start now, because it takes most people many months.
  2. Search the Federal Employment Agency’s job portal and the Make it in Germany job listings for “Ausbildung” places that accept international applicants.
  3. Apply directly to the companies with a German CV and cover letter.
  4. Once you have a contract, book your visa appointment at the German embassy or consulate.

Real German companies don’t charge you for a training place. Be careful with agents who ask for large fees to “guarantee” an Ausbildung. Read how to spot fake job abroad offers.

Already have a degree or a recognised qualification? Compare Germany’s skilled worker routes and the Opportunity Card.

title: Schengen visa for Africans in 2026: fees, documents and how early to apply
description: One Schengen visa lets you visit 29 European countries for up to 90 days. Here's which embassy to apply to, the €90 fee, the documents you need and how early to apply.

facts.label: Fee
facts.value: €90 for adults, €45 for children aged 6 to 12, plus the visa centre's service fee

facts.label: When to apply
facts.value: No earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before you travel

facts.label: Decision
facts.value: Usually 15 days, up to 45 days

facts.label: Passport
facts.value: Valid for at least 3 months after you leave the Schengen area

body:
A Schengen visa is a short-stay visa for visits of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. One visa covers all 29 Schengen countries, including France, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Switzerland. Citizens of Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia all need one to visit.

It’s for tourism, family visits, business meetings and conferences. It doesn’t let you work or study long-term. For that you need a national visa from the country, such as Germany’s Opportunity Card.

Which embassy to apply to

  • If you’re visiting one country, apply to that country’s embassy or consulate.
  • If you’re visiting several, apply to the country where you’ll spend the most time.
  • If you’ll spend the same time in each, apply to the country you’ll enter first.

You normally apply in the country where you legally live. Most embassies use a visa centre, such as VFS Global, TLScontact or BLS International, to take applications. Your embassy’s website says which one it uses.

Fees

  • €90 for adults.
  • €45 for children aged 6 to 12.
  • Children under 6 don’t pay the visa fee.

You pay in local currency. The visa centre adds its own service fee on top.

When to apply

You can apply up to 6 months before your trip, and at least 15 days before. Appointments can be hard to get in busy seasons such as summer and December, so book as soon as your dates are firm.

Most decisions take 15 days. If the embassy needs to look more closely or asks for more documents, it can take up to 45 days.

Documents you need

  • A passport valid for at least 3 months after you leave the Schengen area, issued within the last 10 years, with two blank pages.
  • The completed application form.
  • A recent passport photo that meets ICAO standards.
  • Travel medical insurance covering emergency care, hospital treatment and repatriation, with at least €30,000 of cover.
  • Proof of why you’re travelling, such as an invitation letter, a conference registration or a tour booking.
  • Proof of accommodation, such as hotel bookings or a host’s invitation.
  • Proof you can pay for the trip, such as recent bank statements and payslips.
  • Proof you’ll come home, such as a letter from your employer approving your leave, your business registration, or your school enrolment.

You give your fingerprints when you apply, unless you’re exempt. Each embassy can ask for more documents, so always check its own checklist.

Tips that help your application

  • Be consistent. Your bank statements, leave letter and booking dates should all match your travel plan.
  • Show steady money, not a sudden deposit. A large deposit just before you apply raises questions.
  • Never use fake documents. A fake bank statement or booking can get you refused and can lead to a ban. Anyone selling a “guaranteed visa” is a scammer. Read how to spot fake visa offers.
  • Build a travel history. People who used past visas properly are more likely to get longer, multiple-entry visas later.

At the border

Since 10 April 2026, the EU’s Entry/Exit System (EES) records your fingerprints, photo and entry and exit dates at the border instead of stamping your passport. It keeps count of your 90 days, so don’t overstay.

You may also hear about ETIAS. It’s a travel authorisation for people who don’t need a visa, such as Americans. If you need a Schengen visa, you don’t need ETIAS.

title: UK Graduate visa: apply by 31 December 2026 to keep the 2-year stay
description: From 1 January 2027 the UK Graduate visa drops from 2 years to 18 months for bachelor's and master's graduates. Here's who qualifies, what it costs and how to apply in time.

facts.label: Stay
facts.value: 2 years if you apply by 31 December 2026, 18 months from 1 January 2027 (3 years after a PhD)

facts.label: Fee
facts.value: £937, plus a health surcharge of £1,035 a year

facts.label: Decision
facts.value: Usually within 8 weeks

facts.label: Extension
facts.value: Not possible, but you can switch to a Skilled Worker visa

body:
If you’re finishing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in the UK, the date you apply for your Graduate visa now matters:

  • Apply on or before 31 December 2026 and you get 2 years to live and work in the UK.
  • Apply from 1 January 2027 and you get 18 months.
  • PhD and other doctoral graduates keep 3 years either way.

The new rule depends on the date you submit your application, not the date your course started.

Who can apply

You can apply if all of these are true:

  • You’re in the UK on a Student visa (or an older Tier 4 (General) student visa), and it hasn’t expired yet.
  • You studied a UK bachelor’s, master’s or PhD, or another eligible course such as a PGCE, PGDE or some law courses.
  • Your university has told the Home Office you completed your course. You don’t have to wait for your graduation ceremony or certificate.
  • Your university is listed as a “Student Sponsor - Track Record” on the Home Office register.

You also need enough time in the UK:

  • If your course was longer than 12 months, you must have studied in the UK for at least 12 months.
  • If your course was 12 months or shorter, you must have studied in the UK for the whole course.

To beat the 31 December cut-off, ask your international student office when they’ll report your completion to the Home Office. You can’t apply until they do.

How much it costs

  • Application fee: £937.
  • Immigration Health Surcharge: £1,035 for each year of the visa, so £2,070 for a 2-year visa.

Your partner and children each pay their own application fee and surcharge.

Documents you need

  • Your passport.
  • The CAS reference number from your Student visa application. Your university can find it if you’ve lost it.
  • Your biometric residence permit (BRP), if you have one. You can use it until 24 months after the expiry date on the card, or until 31 December 2026, whichever comes first.
  • A letter from your scholarship or sponsor approving the application, if they paid both your course fees and your living costs in the last 12 months.
  • Certified translations of anything not in English or Welsh.

On a scholarship that requires you to go home, such as Chevening, you’re expected to return for at least 2 years after your award. Read your scholarship’s rules before you apply. See what happens after you apply for Chevening.

Your partner and children

Your partner and children can stay with you, but they usually must already be your dependants on your Student visa. A child born in the UK while you’re on a Student or Graduate visa is the main exception.

New dependants can’t join you on a Graduate visa. They may be able to join you later if you switch to a work visa such as the Skilled Worker visa.

How to apply

  1. Check that your university has reported your completion.
  2. Apply online on GOV.UK before your Student visa expires.
  3. Prove your identity with the UK Immigration: ID Check app, or by giving your fingerprints and photo at a UKVCAS service point. You’ll be told which one to use.
  4. Don’t travel outside the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man until you get a decision, or your application will be withdrawn.
  5. You’ll usually get a decision within 8 weeks. If you’re approved, you get an eVisa, which you view in your UKVI account.

What you can do on a Graduate visa

You can work in most jobs, look for work, be self-employed and volunteer. You can’t claim most public benefits or work as a professional sportsperson.

You can’t extend a Graduate visa. Use the time to find an employer who can sponsor you, then switch to a Skilled Worker visa before it runs out. Read the UK Skilled Worker visa rules for 2026 to check the salary you’ll need.

title: Australia Awards Africa: how to prepare for the round opening 1 February 2027
description: Australia Awards pays for a full master's degree in Australia for African professionals. The next round opens on 1 February 2027. Here's who can apply, what it covers and how to get ready now.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Master's at an Australian university

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Citizens of 25 African countries, including Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Zimbabwe and Zambia

facts.label: Next round
facts.value: Opens 1 February 2027 (the last round closed on 30 April)

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: Full tuition, flights, living costs, health cover and an arrival allowance

body:
Australia Awards is one of the few fully funded scholarships built for working professionals in Africa. It pays for a full master’s degree in Australia, and it’s open to citizens of all six countries we cover.

The next application round opens on 1 February 2027. The last round ran from 1 February to 30 April 2026, so expect a window of about three months. The best applicants start preparing now.

Who can apply

These are the rules from the last round (for study starting in 2027). Check the new profile when the round opens, as details can change.

  • Citizenship: you’re a citizen of an eligible country and apply from that country. The 25 countries include Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Zimbabwe and Zambia.
  • Age: at least 25 years old on 1 February of the year your study starts.
  • Work experience: at least 5 years’ work experience after your first degree, in a field related to what you want to study, and you’re employed when you apply.
  • Education: you have a bachelor’s degree, and you don’t already have (or aren’t studying for) a master’s.
  • English: IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0, or the same level in TOEFL or PTE, valid on 1 January of the year you start. There’s an exemption if English is your first language and you studied in English.
  • Previous awards: you haven’t had a long-term Australia Award before.

What it covers

  • Full tuition fees
  • Return flights
  • A contribution to living costs
  • A one-off allowance when you arrive
  • Overseas Student Health Cover
  • An introductory academic programme and extra academic support
  • Fieldwork costs for research and some coursework master’s

Australia Awards scholars must leave Australia when they finish and spend at least two years outside it, so the scholarship suits people who want to use the degree at home.

Priority study areas

The last round prioritised:

  • agriculture and food security
  • climate change
  • foreign policy and international security
  • gender, disability and social inclusion
  • mining and energy

Your application is stronger when your course and your plan clearly fit one of these.

Get ready now: a timeline

WhenWhat to do
November to December 2026Take IELTS if you need it (IELTS fees in Nigeria). Choose 2 or 3 courses in Australia.
December 2026 to January 2027Get certified copies of your degree and transcripts. Ask your employer for a letter that confirms your role and dates.
January 2027Draft your answers about your work, the course and your plan after it. See how to write a strong statement.
1 February 2027The round opens. Read the new profile and apply online through OASIS.
Before the deadlineSubmit early. Late applications aren’t considered.

If you’re shortlisted, you’ll be invited to an interview.

Other options

If you don’t have 5 years’ experience yet, look at awards with lower experience rules in our 2027 scholarship calendar, such as Gates Cambridge or Erasmus Mundus.

Australia Awards is free to apply for. Never pay anyone who promises to get you selected.

title: Duolingo English Test or IELTS: which should you take in 2026?
description: The Duolingo English Test costs $70 and you take it at home, but many visas don't accept it. Here's where it works, where you need IELTS, and how to choose.

facts.label: Duolingo English Test
facts.value: US$70, about 1 hour, taken at home, valid 2 years

facts.label: IELTS in Nigeria
facts.value: ₦299,000 for Academic or General Training

facts.label: Rule of thumb
facts.value: Duolingo for admission only; IELTS if you'll need a visa or work permit that names it

body:
The Duolingo English Test is cheaper and easier to book than IELTS, so many students ask if they can skip IELTS completely. The honest answer: sometimes. It depends on whether you only need a university admission, or also a visa that names its own list of English tests.

The two tests at a glance

Duolingo English TestIELTS
PriceUS$70₦299,000 in Nigeria (see current fees)
Where you take itAt home, on your own computerAt a test centre
LengthAbout 1 hourAbout 2 hours 45 minutes in total, including speaking
ResultsUsually within 2 daysA few days on computer, about 13 days on paper
Score10 to 160Band 1 to 9
Valid for2 years2 years for most universities and visas

Where the Duolingo English Test works

  • Many universities. A large number of universities accept it for admission, including many in the USA, Canada and Ireland, and some in the UK. Always check your course page, because some universities and courses don’t.
  • US student visas (F-1). There’s no single US government list: your university sets the English requirement for your I-20.
  • Canadian study permits. IRCC doesn’t name a language test for most study permits, so the university’s requirement is what counts.
  • Irish study visas. Ireland lists it among the English tests it accepts for study visas.

Where you need IELTS (or another approved test)

  • UK visas that need a SELT. The Duolingo English Test isn’t a UK Secure English Language Test. You can’t use it for a Skilled Worker or Health and Care visa, or for study below degree level. For a degree, your university may assess your English itself and accept it, but only if that university says so.
  • Canada Express Entry and permanent residence. IRCC only accepts CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training or PTE Core for English. Note that IELTS Academic doesn’t count here.
  • Australia and New Zealand visas. Neither accepts tests taken at home.
  • Nursing registration. The UK’s NMC and Ireland’s NMBI ask for IELTS Academic or OET. See how nurses can work in the UK or Ireland.

How to choose

  • Applying only for admission at universities that accept it: take the Duolingo English Test. It’s cheaper and faster.
  • Planning to work, move with family or apply for residence later in the UK, Canada, Australia or New Zealand: take IELTS (UKVI version for UK visas, General Training for Canada PR), so you only pay once.
  • Applying for a scholarship: check its own rules. Some, such as Australia Awards, name IELTS, TOEFL or PTE.

Tips for the Duolingo English Test

  • Use a quiet room, a laptop with a working camera and microphone, and a stable internet connection. A dropped connection can cancel your result.
  • Read the rules before you start: you can’t use headphones, notes or a second screen, and you must look at the screen.
  • Take the free practice test on the official site first, so the question types don’t surprise you.

Requirements change, so confirm on your university’s page and the official immigration website before you book.

title: Ireland's Critical Skills Employment Permit: salary rules, jobs and family in 2026
description: Ireland's Critical Skills permit lets skilled workers from Africa bring their family straight away and move to residence after two years. Here are the 2026 salary rules, fees and how to apply.

facts.label: Minimum salary
facts.value: €40,904 for jobs on the Critical Skills list (with a relevant degree), €68,911 for most other jobs

facts.label: Recent graduates
facts.value: €36,848 if you qualified in the last 12 months

facts.label: Fee
facts.value: €1,000, with 90% back if refused

facts.label: Family
facts.value: Can join you straight away, and your spouse can work

body:
Ireland is one of the best English-speaking countries for skilled workers right now. Its Critical Skills Employment Permit is aimed at jobs Ireland can’t fill locally, such as IT, engineering, nursing and medicine. It also lets your family come with you from the start.

Salary rules from 1 March 2026

You need a job offer that pays at least:

  • €40,904 a year for a job on Ireland’s Critical Skills Occupations List, where the job needs a relevant degree or higher, or
  • €36,848 a year for the same jobs if you got your qualification in the last 12 months, or
  • €68,911 a year for almost any other job, unless it’s on Ireland’s list of ineligible jobs.

Nurses and midwives need a qualification accepted by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI). See how nurses can work in the UK or Ireland.

If your job isn’t on the list and pays less than €68,911, look at Ireland’s General Employment Permit, which starts at €36,605. We compare both in moving abroad beyond Canada.

Jobs on the Critical Skills list

The list is based on Ireland’s skills shortages. It includes many:

  • ICT professionals, such as software developers, data and cloud roles,
  • professional engineers and technologists,
  • doctors, nurses and other health professionals.

Check the full, current list on the official page before you apply, as it’s reviewed regularly.

The job offer

  • The offer must be for at least 2 years.
  • You’re expected to stay with your first employer for at least 9 months, unless you’re made redundant or the job changes completely.
  • Your employer can’t make you pay back the permit fee.

Fees

The permit costs €1,000. If it’s refused, 90% is refunded. You’ll also pay for your visa (if you need one) and for your residence registration after you arrive.

Family

This is where the Critical Skills permit beats most work visas:

  • Your spouse or partner and children can apply to join you straight away.
  • Once they live in Ireland, your spouse or partner can work in any job, with a free Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit.

Path to residence

When your permit ends, usually after 2 years, you can apply to the Department of Justice for Stamp 4 permission. With Stamp 4, you can work for any employer without a permit. After 5 years (60 months) of permission, you can apply for long-term residence.

How to get started

  1. Check your job is on the Critical Skills list, or that your offer pays at least €68,911.
  2. Search for jobs with Irish employers that sponsor permits, and apply directly on their websites.
  3. Once you have an offer, you or your employer applies online through the Department’s employment permits system.
  4. After the permit is granted, apply for your visa if your nationality needs one.

Never pay a recruiter to “buy” an Irish job or permit. Real Irish employers don’t charge for jobs. Read how to spot fake job abroad offers before you send money to anyone.

title: Proof of funds for a student visa in 2026: UK, Canada and Germany
description: How much money you must show for a student visa to the UK, Canada or Germany in 2026, how long it must sit in your account, and how to avoid the mistakes that get visas refused.

facts.label: UK
facts.value: £1,529 a month in London or £1,171 elsewhere, for up to 9 months, plus first-year fees

facts.label: Canada
facts.value: CAD 23,448 for one person (from 1 September 2026), plus tuition and travel

facts.label: Germany
facts.value: €11,904 a year, usually in a blocked account

body:
Getting a university offer is only half the journey. To get a student visa, you must also prove you can pay for your studies and your living costs, and each country has its own amount and rules.

Here’s what the UK, Canada and Germany ask for in 2026, and how to prepare your bank statements so they don’t get your visa refused.

UK Student visa

For living costs, you must show:

  • £1,529 a month if you’ll study in London, or
  • £1,171 a month anywhere else in the UK,

for up to 9 months. That’s up to £13,761 for London and £10,539 elsewhere. You also need enough to pay your first year’s course fees, which are shown on your CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies), minus anything you’ve already paid.

The money must have been in your account for at least 28 days in a row, and the end of that 28-day period must be within 31 days of the day you apply. You need extra money for each family member you bring.

If your money is in naira, cedis, shillings or rand, keep a buffer above the minimum, because the amount is checked in pounds and exchange rates move.

Official: GOV.UK, money you need for a Student visa

Canada study permit

For study permit applications received on or after 1 September 2026, you must show CAD 23,448 for one person for a year of living costs, outside Quebec. Applications before that date needed CAD 22,895.

This amount doesn’t include tuition or travel: you must show your first year’s tuition and your travel costs on top. Bringing family raises the amount; IRCC publishes a table by family size. Quebec sets its own amounts.

IRCC accepts several kinds of proof, including:

  • bank statements for the past 6 months, showing where the money came from,
  • a guaranteed investment certificate (GIC) from a Canadian bank,
  • receipts for tuition and housing already paid,
  • a scholarship or student loan letter,
  • a letter from a sponsor, with their job, income and ID.

Official: IRCC, proof of financial support

Before you choose Canada, read what the study permit cap means for African students.

Germany student visa

Germany expects you to show €11,904 for a year of study, about €992 a month. Most students do this with a blocked account (Sperrkonto): you deposit the full amount before your visa appointment, and once you’re in Germany you can take out a fixed amount each month.

Other accepted proof includes:

  • a scholarship award letter from a recognised scholarship provider,
  • a formal guarantee from someone who lives permanently in Germany,
  • proof of your parents’ income and assets.

Embassies sometimes ask for a different amount, so confirm with the German embassy or consulate in your country before you pay into a blocked account.

Official: Study in Germany (DAAD), proof of financing

Mistakes that get visas refused

  • Money that appears just before you apply. A large deposit with no clear source looks borrowed. Keep the money in the account early, and be ready to show where it came from, such as salary, business income or the sale of property.
  • Statements that don’t meet the rules. Each country has rules on dates, names and stamps. Check them before you print.
  • Sponsors with no proof. If a parent or relative is paying, include their letter, ID, proof of relationship and their own bank statements.
  • Forgetting fees. The UK and Canada both expect tuition on top of living costs.
  • Paying an “agent” to provide funds. Fake or rented statements can get you banned from reapplying. See how to spot fake job and visa offers.

Scholarships change everything

A fully funded scholarship usually counts as proof of funds. See the awards open to Africans in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

Amounts change often, so always check the official page on the day you apply.

title: How to write a statement of purpose that wins scholarships
description: A clear, step-by-step way to write a statement of purpose or scholarship essay, with a structure that works, mistakes that sink applications, and a checklist before you submit.

facts.label: Length
facts.value: Usually 500 to 1,000 words, or exactly the limit the form gives

facts.label: Time to write
facts.value: Start 4 to 6 weeks before the deadline

facts.label: Golden rule
facts.value: Write a new one for every course and scholarship

body:
Your statement of purpose is often the only place a scholarship committee hears your voice. Grades and references show what you’ve done. The statement shows where you’re going, and why giving you the money makes sense.

Most applications from Africa are turned down for the same few reasons: the statement is generic, it tells a long life story, or it never says what the applicant will do after the course. This guide shows you how to avoid all three.

What the committee wants to know

Every good statement answers five questions:

  1. What do you want to study? Name the course, not just the field.
  2. Why this course and this university? Mention modules, research groups or teachers that match your plans.
  3. What have you done so far? Your degree, work, projects and results, with numbers where you can.
  4. What will you do after? A specific job, project or change you’ll make at home.
  5. Why you? What makes you more likely than other applicants to use this chance well.

If a paragraph doesn’t answer one of these, cut it.

A structure that works

Opening (one short paragraph). Start with the problem you want to solve, not your childhood. For example: “In my three years as a nurse in Kano, I saw mothers travel 60 km for a scan that could be done in their village.”

Your background (two paragraphs). What you studied, what you’ve done at work, and what you achieved. Use evidence: “I trained 14 health workers” beats “I am passionate about health”.

Why this course (one or two paragraphs). Link the course to your plan. Name two or three modules, a professor’s research or a practical part of the course, and say how each one helps.

Your plan after the course (one paragraph). Be specific about the role, the organisation or the project, and what will change because of it. Scholarships funded by governments and foundations especially want to see that you’ll use the skills at home.

Closing (two or three sentences). Bring it back to the problem from your opening, and say in one line why you’re ready.

Mistakes that sink applications

  • One statement for every application. Committees can tell. Change the course, university and plan for each one.
  • Starting with “Since I was a child”. It wastes your best lines. Start with the problem or your work.
  • Lists of qualities. “Hardworking, passionate and dedicated” says nothing. Show it with an example.
  • No plan after the course. This is the most common reason strong candidates lose.
  • Copying templates or letting AI write it. Reviewers read thousands of statements, and copied or machine-written text sounds the same. Use tools to check grammar, but the story and the plan must be yours.
  • Ignoring the word limit. Going over can get you rejected before anyone reads it.

Scholarship essays are different

Some scholarships ask several short questions instead of one statement, for example about leadership, networking or your career plan. Answer each question directly, and use a different example in each answer. The same five questions above still apply, just spread across the answers.

Before you submit: a checklist

  • It names the exact course and university.
  • Every paragraph answers one of the five questions.
  • There’s at least one number or result in your background section.
  • Your plan after the course is specific enough that someone could check it in five years.
  • Someone who knows your field has read it, and someone outside your field understood it.
  • It’s within the word limit, with no spelling mistakes.

Where to use it

Your statement is ready to adapt for the big awards in our 2027 scholarship calendar, including Gates Cambridge, Erasmus Mundus and DAAD EPOS. Check each scholarship’s own instructions for length and questions, as they differ.

title: Germany Is Looking for Skilled Workers. Could You Qualify?
description: Germany is hiring skilled workers from outside Europe. Here are the four main routes, the 2026 salary for the EU Blue Card, and the first steps for Nigerians, Kenyans, Ghanaians and South Africans.

facts.label: Main routes
facts.value: EU Blue Card, skilled worker visa, Opportunity Card

facts.label: Blue Card salary
facts.value: €50,700 a year in 2026, or €45,934.20 in shortage jobs

facts.label: Key step
facts.value: Get your degree or training recognised in Germany

facts.label: Language
facts.value: German helps most; some IT and research jobs use English

body:
Germany has more jobs than workers in many fields, and it has changed its immigration rules to bring in people from outside Europe. Nurses, engineers, IT specialists, electricians and other trained workers from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia can all apply.

You don’t need to know someone in Germany, and you don’t pay an agent. But you do need the right qualification, and for most routes, a job offer first.

The four main routes

1. EU Blue Card. For people with a university degree and a job offer that pays enough. In 2026 the salary is €50,700 a year, or €45,934.20 for shortage jobs such as IT, engineering, medicine and nursing, and for graduates in their first three years after their degree. IT specialists with 3 years’ experience can qualify without a degree. The Blue Card is the fastest way to permanent residence.

2. Skilled worker visa. For people with a recognised degree or at least two years of vocational training (for example, electricians, plumbers, mechanics or nurses) and a job offer in their field. There’s no fixed salary for most applicants under 45.

3. Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte). Lets you move to Germany for up to a year without a job offer to look for one, and work part-time while you search. It uses a points system. See our full guide to the Opportunity Card.

4. Recognition partnership. If your qualification is only partly recognised, an employer can hire you while you complete the missing training in Germany.

Salary figures for 2026 were published by the German government in late 2025. When we checked, the Make it in Germany page still showed the 2025 amounts (€48,300 and €43,759.80), so confirm the current figure there before you apply.

Could you qualify? A quick check

You have a good chance if you can say yes to most of these:

  • I have a university degree, or at least two years of formal vocational training.
  • I have worked in my field for at least two years.
  • I’m learning German, or I already speak it at A2 or higher.
  • My job is one Germany is short of: nursing and care, IT, engineering, skilled trades, or teaching.

If you’re missing the job offer, the Opportunity Card is built for you. If you’re missing the qualification, a German vocational training place (Ausbildung) is another way in.

Get your qualification recognised first

This is the step most people skip, and it’s the reason many visa applications fail. The German Foreign Office says that without recognition of your foreign degree or certificate, your visa application can’t be processed.

  • Degrees: check whether your university and degree are listed in the anabin database. For many non-regulated jobs, that’s enough.
  • Regulated jobs (nursing, medicine, teaching and some others): you need permission to practise from the German authority for that job.
  • Vocational training: apply for recognition through the Recognition in Germany portal, which shows which office handles your job.

How to apply

  1. Check your route on Make it in Germany, the German government’s official site for skilled workers.
  2. Start recognition of your qualification.
  3. Learn German. Even A2 makes job hunting much easier.
  4. Apply for jobs on the Federal Employment Agency’s job board and on Make it in Germany.
  5. Once you have an offer, book a national visa appointment at the German embassy in your country and bring the employer’s “Declaration regarding a contract of employment”.

Avoid the scams

Real German employers don’t charge you for a job or a visa. Be careful with anyone who promises a guaranteed job, asks for money for a “work permit”, or wants payment before an interview. Read how to spot a fake job abroad offer before you pay anyone.

Nurses should also read how nurses from Africa can work in the UK or Ireland to compare their options.

title: Thinking of Moving Abroad? Look Beyond Canada
description: Canada is cutting the number of newcomers it lets in, but it isn't the only option. Here's how Germany, the UK, Ireland and Australia compare for skilled workers from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa.

facts.label: Germany
facts.value: EU Blue Card from €50,700 (2026), or a 1-year job-search visa

facts.label: UK
facts.value: Skilled Worker visa from £41,700, degree-level jobs, B2 English

facts.label: Ireland
facts.value: Critical Skills permit from €40,904, General permit from €36,605

facts.label: Australia
facts.value: Skills in Demand visa from AUD 79,499 (from 1 July 2026)

body:
For years, Canada was the first choice for Nigerians, Kenyans, Ghanaians and South Africans planning to move abroad. That has changed. Canada is issuing fewer study permits and cutting the number of temporary residents, so competition for every place is tougher.

Canada is still worth considering, but it shouldn’t be your only plan. Several other countries are actively hiring skilled workers from Africa, and some are easier to reach.

Germany: the most open door right now

Germany is short of workers in nursing, IT, engineering and skilled trades, and it has made its rules simpler.

  • EU Blue Card: for graduates with a job offer paying at least €50,700 a year in 2026, or €45,934.20 in shortage jobs.
  • Skilled worker visa: for people with a recognised degree or vocational training and a job offer.
  • Opportunity Card: move for up to a year without a job offer to look for work.

The catch is language: most jobs need some German. Read our guide to whether you could qualify for Germany.

United Kingdom: harder than before, still open

The UK Skilled Worker visa now needs a degree-level job, a salary of at least £41,700 (or the job’s going rate) and B2 English. The care worker route has closed to people applying from abroad, but nurses can still go through the Health and Care Worker visa.

See the new UK Skilled Worker rules and what replaced the UK care visa.

Ireland: English-speaking and hiring

Ireland uses employment permits. From 1 March 2026:

  • the Critical Skills Employment Permit needs a salary of at least €40,904, for jobs on Ireland’s critical skills list such as ICT, engineering, nursing and medicine, and
  • the General Employment Permit needs at least €36,605, for most other jobs not on the ineligible list.

Critical Skills holders can bring family and move towards long-term residence. Nurses can register with the NMBI: see how nurses can work in the UK or Ireland.

Australia: high pay, high bar

Australia’s Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) needs an employer sponsor. From 1 July 2026, the Core Skills stream needs a salary of at least AUD 79,499. Australia also runs points-tested permanent visas for people with skills on its occupation lists, but they need strong English and a skills assessment.

For a master’s, Australia Awards Africa funds study for mid-career professionals: see our 2027 scholarship calendar.

How they compare

CountryJob offer first?English only?Best for
GermanyNot with the Opportunity CardUsually no, German helpsNurses, engineers, IT, trades
UKYesYesDegree-level jobs, nurses
IrelandYesYesIT, engineering, health
AustraliaYes, for the 482YesExperienced professionals

Before you go anywhere

  • Use only the official government sites to check the rules. Each country’s visa site is free to read.
  • Never pay for a job offer. Read how to spot a fake job abroad offer.
  • Start your English test or German classes now. They take the longest.

Salary thresholds and rules change every year, so check the official page for each country before you apply.

title: Planning to Study Abroad in 2027? Explore Scholarship Opportunities

If you want to start a master’s, PhD or undergraduate degree abroad in September 2027, now is the time to apply for funding. Most fully funded scholarships close 8 to 12 months before the course starts, and if you miss a window, you wait a full year.

The good news: many of the biggest scholarships are open to students from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia, and they cover tuition, living costs and flights.

Scholarships open now

  • Gates Cambridge: PhD and most one-year master’s courses at the University of Cambridge. Deadlines are 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, depending on the course.
  • Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters: study in two or more European countries, with about €1,400 a month. Each course sets its own deadline, usually between October and January.
  • DAAD EPOS: master’s and PhD courses in Germany for people with at least two years’ work experience. Each course sets its deadline.
  • Mastercard Foundation Scholars: undergraduate and master’s study at partner universities in Africa and abroad.

Opening soon

  • Türkiye Bursları: all levels in Türkiye. The window usually runs from 10 January to 20 February.
  • Australia Awards Africa: master’s in Australia for professionals with at least 5 years’ work experience. The next round opens on 1 February 2027.

See all twelve, with what each covers, in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

Your plan, month by month

WhenWhat to do
Now (October to November)Pick 3 to 5 scholarships and courses. Ask two referees for letters.
November to DecemberTake IELTS or another English test if you need it. Write your statement of purpose.
December to JanuarySubmit applications for Gates Cambridge, Erasmus Mundus and DAAD courses.
January to MarchApply for Türkiye Bursları and Australia Awards. Prepare for interviews.
